questions.prompt: Fructose is ………. times sweeter than sucrose?
questions.explanation: 1.7 is the conventional comparison intended here. Relative sweetness is not a fixed physical constant: concentration, temperature and the testing method alter it.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 57–58.
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2758952/
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Which ones are the ingredients of Aspartame?
questions.explanation: Aspartame is the methyl ester of a dipeptide containing aspartic acid and phenylalanine. The amino-acid pair is C.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 67–68.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Which one decreases the absorption of Iron?
questions.explanation: D is the intended dietary inhibitor among these choices. Phytate and other compounds in some fiber-rich foods inhibit nonheme-iron absorption; it is not true that every purified fiber has this effect. Vitamin C and gastric acidity favor absorption.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 261–265.
https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Iron-HealthProfessional/
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of TX/LT (respectively)?
options: Increasing the clotting/Increasing the chemotaxy of neutrophils
Increasing the chemotaxy of neutrophils/Increasing the clotting
questions.explanation: Thromboxane A2 promotes platelet aggregation; leukotriene B4 is a neutrophil chemoattractant. Different leukotrienes also have other actions, so LT here refers principally to LTB4.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 88–89.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: The percentage of calcium absorption is……….
questions.explanation: About 25% is the closest conventional adult estimate among these choices. Fractional absorption varies with dose, age, vitamin D status and physiologic demand; it is not universally 25%.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 254–257.
https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: What is the ultimate function of PTH?
questions.explanation: Parathyroid hormone raises circulating calcium through renal calcium retention, calcitriol-mediated intestinal absorption and, when needed, mobilization from bone.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 254–257.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Keshan disease is a situation of ………
questions.explanation: Keshan disease is an endemic cardiomyopathy associated with selenium deficiency, interacting with other environmental or infectious factors.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF p. 267.
https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Selenium-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: What is the main function of vitamin B6?
questions.explanation: Pyridoxal phosphate is the coenzyme for aminotransferases. B6 participates in many amino-acid reactions, but transamination is the best listed answer.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 228–229.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: What is the main cause of Beriberi disease?
questions.explanation: Beriberi is caused by thiamine deficiency; dry and wet forms emphasize neurologic and cardiovascular manifestations respectively.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 225–226.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: What is the main cause of Pellagra disease?
questions.explanation: Pellagra results from inadequate niacin availability, including inadequate tryptophan contribution, and classically causes dermatitis, diarrhea and dementia.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 227–228.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: What is the main cause of photophobia?
questions.explanation: Riboflavin deficiency can cause ocular symptoms including sensitivity to light. It is the best of the nutritional options, not the main cause of photophobia in clinical practice overall.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 226–227.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Which one is the site of vitamin B12 absorption?
questions.explanation: The intrinsic-factor–B12 complex is absorbed by receptor-mediated uptake in the distal ileum; the stomach supplies intrinsic factor but is not the uptake site.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 230–232.
https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminB12-HealthProfessional/
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of folic acid or vitamin B12 causes?
questions.explanation: Either deficiency can impair DNA synthesis and produce megaloblastic anemia. B12 deficiency also causes neurologic injury, which folate alone does not prevent.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 230–232.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Which vitamins are hormone-like compounds?
questions.explanation: Calcitriol and retinoic acid act through nuclear receptors to regulate gene expression, explaining the hormone-like description of vitamins D and A.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 212–221.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: Which listed amino acid is the precursor for serotonin synthesis?
questions.explanation: Tryptophan is the precursor of serotonin. The repaired stem tests this biochemical pathway, not an unsupported claim that tryptophan supplements reliably improve mood or treat mood disorders.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 109–113.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key. Edited study version tests the biochemical precursor; original retained.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin A metabolite chiefly regulates gene expression and epithelial differentiation?

questions.prompt: What is the most prevalent age for Rickets?
questions.explanation: The supplied key selects 1–2 years, a common period of presentation during rapid early growth. Nutritional rickets also occurs in younger infants and adolescents; there is no universal prevalence peak for every population.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 218–221.
https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241516587

questions.prompt: Which one is recommended more in order to reduce blood cholesterol levels?
options: None of the items mentioned above
questions.explanation: Viscous soluble fiber such as pectin can lower LDL cholesterol. Omega-3 fatty acids primarily lower triglycerides; exercise remains beneficial but is not the most direct cholesterol-lowering mechanism offered.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 69–74, 576–585.
questions.note: Source green highlighting is preserved as a supplied answer, not independently authenticated as an official university key.

questions.prompt: How much extra vitamin C per day is recommended for adults who smoke, above the nonsmoker age/sex-specific RDA?
questions.explanation: The source marks 90 mg/day, but smokers require an extra 35 mg/day above the age/sex-specific nonsmoker RDA. The repaired question asks for that increment.
evidence: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/
DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 232–234.

questions.prompt: Which listed mineral supplement can cause iron-overload toxicity when taken unnecessarily in high doses by an iron-replete person?
questions.explanation: Unnecessary iron in an iron-replete person can cause harm; iron overload promotes tissue injury. Cancer or cardiovascular disease alone is not a blanket reason to withhold medically indicated iron. The study wording specifies excess iron without deficiency.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 263–265.
https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Iron-HealthProfessional/

questions.prompt: Which listed food contains enough vitamin K that a person taking warfarin should keep its intake consistent rather than abruptly change it?
questions.explanation: Cabbage supplies vitamin K. Warfarin users should keep vitamin K intake consistent rather than automatically avoid all vitamin-K-containing foods. The study wording corrects that unsafe blanket advice.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 448–449.
